summary: Add a frequency–time sketch and its underlying wavefront reasoning to strengthen the otherwise well-covered Doppler chapter.

improvements.why: ER 9702 w23 P21 Q5 reports difficulty sketching observed frequency above the source frequency before passing and below it afterwards; the note has no diagram.
improvements.what: Use graph_sketch for observed frequency $f_o$ against time for a source passing a stationary observer at constant speed along a direct line: labelled source-frequency $f_s$ reference, higher approach level and lower recession level, with the passing instant marked. Embed and explain what to notice; avoid implying sound speed changes.

improvements.why: Existing conceptual practice is mainly MCQs and has no Sketch command-word task, despite the examiner-reported graph difficulty.
improvements.what: Add an exam-style structured Sketch item asking for $f_o$ versus time as a constant-speed sound source approaches, passes and recedes from a stationary observer, with $f_s$ marked; scheme credits the higher approach frequency, lower recession frequency and correctly labelled passing instant.

improvements.why: The note states the sign rule but skips the quantitative wavefront-spacing step that explains the denominator.
improvements.what: Add a compact derivation using emission period $T=1/f_s$: consecutive wavefront spacing is $(v-v_s)T$ ahead and $(v+v_s)T$ behind, then $f_o=v/\lambda$ gives the two formulas. State the stationary observer and same-medium assumptions.
